adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` attempts to express “any key with a number value” via object literal computed keys: `{ [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), ... }`. Zod `z.object({...})` does not support wildcard/dynamic keys this way; it will instead define a single literal property whose name is whatever `z.string().toString()` returns (not a real wildcard). As a result, in “sync mode” (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`) the schema will not validate `expiry_date` (or any actual expiry field) as intended, and will likely fail parsing unless the response contains that exact literal key.

Webhook auth secret comparison is not constant-time and misconfigured header name env var can cause every request to 403 with no clear error

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the webhook auth check uses `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. This is (1) a non-constant-time secret comparison (plain `!==` on strings) and (2) the header lookup is effectively case-sensitive because Node/Next normalizes `req.headers` keys to lowercase, but the env var is not normalized (so a value like `Calcom-Webhook-Secret` would yield `undefined` and always 403). The response only says `Invalid webhook secret`, giving no indication the header name itself is misconfigured.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Credential-sharing mode replaces app-specific schemas with the minimum schema, so tokens from the remote sync endpoint are stored into user credentials without app-specific validation, enabling credential data injection

adjudication.rationale: In credential-sharing mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), `parseRefreshTokenResponse` validates refresh responses with `minimumTokenResponseSchema` instead of the app-specific schema passed in (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`). That minimum schema allows unknown extra fields and only requires `access_token` (and any numeric fields), so a remote sync endpoint response can bypass app-specific validation. Call sites then persist/merge this minimally-validated data into credentials (e.g., Office365: `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)` followed by `prisma.credential.update`, in `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`). This is a real, diff-grounded weakening of validation for remotely-sourced token data and can allow malformed/unexpected fields to be stored into user credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse sets refresh_token to the literal string 'refresh_token' when missing, overwriting the user's real refresh token in the O365 flow with junk

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when `refresh_token` is missing it is forcibly set to the literal string `"refresh_token"` (`refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`). In the O365 refresh flow (`packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`), the returned `tokenResponse.data` is spread over existing `o365AuthCredentials` (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`), so this dummy value will overwrite a previously valid `o365AuthCredentials.refresh_token` and then be persisted via `prisma.credential.update`, causing real refresh tokens to be replaced with junk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time !== instead of crypto.timingSafeEqual, allowing timing side channels

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the secret check uses a direct `!==` comparison between `req.headers[...]` and `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. This introduces a potential timing side-channel for a secret value and is typically mitigated by constant-time comparison (e.g., `crypto.timingSafeEqual`) when verifying shared secrets.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inbound credential webhook relies only on a shared secret with no per-request signature, replay protection, per-user/per-app scoping, or rate limiting, allowing anyone with the secret to overwrite any user's credentials

adjudication.rationale: The new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` authorizes requests solely by comparing a static shared secret in a request header (`req.headers[CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME]` vs `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). After that, it trusts `userId` and `appSlug` from the body and performs a `credential.update`/`credential.create` for that `userId` + `appId` (derived from `appMetadata.slug`). There is no per-request signature/HMAC, nonce/timestamp/replay protection, user/app scoping tied to the secret, or any rate limiting in this diff. Therefore, anyone who obtains/leaks the shared secret can overwrite credentials for arbitrary users/apps by choosing `userId`/`appSlug` in the body, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Outbound sync fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends no authentication (no secret, HMAC, or auth header), so the parent app cannot verify requests came from Cal.com

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, it `fetch`es `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with only a POST body (`calcomUserId`, `appSlug`) and sets no authentication header/secret/HMAC. The diff introduces webhook secret validation for inbound sync (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) but does not attach any comparable secret to outbound sync, so the receiving “parent app” endpoint cannot authenticate that the request originated from Cal.com based on this request alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce refreshes tokens unconditionally in the constructor path with no expiry check and doesn't use refreshOAuthTokens, silently breaking credential-sharing and risking provider throttling; it also discards extra fields in credential.key when updating

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code now refreshes the Salesforce access token via a direct `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` on the service initialization path (immediately after reading `credential.key`), with no conditional/expiry check shown. Unlike other integrations in this diff, Salesforce does not use the newly introduced `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`, so when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` + `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, it will still hit Salesforce directly instead of the sync endpoint, undermining the credential-sharing behavior. Additionally, the update `data: { key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token } }` writes only the fields defined in `salesforceTokenSchema` (plus `refresh_token`), dropping any other existing fields that may have been present in `credential.key`, which is a verifiable potential data-loss regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unhandled zod.parse and JSON.parse of decrypted keys in app-credential webhook throw 500s instead of 400s on malformed input

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler uses `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` and later `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` without any try/catch or safeParse. If the request body is malformed or the decrypted payload is not valid JSON, these will throw and (per Next.js API route behavior) result in an unhandled exception/500 response rather than a controlled 400-series error. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME used unvalidated as header lookup without .toLowerCase(), silently failing all requests if env var contains whitespace or caps

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the code indexes `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]` without normalizing the env-provided header name. Node/Next lowercases incoming header keys, so if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` contains uppercase characters or whitespace, the lookup will likely return `undefined` and the request will be rejected with 403 (`Invalid webhook secret`). The `.env.example` comment says it "Should be in lowercase", but the code doesn’t enforce/trim/lowercase it, making this a configuration footgun rather than an intrinsic defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce CalendarService unconditionally refreshes tokens (blocking fetch + DB write) on every instantiation with no expiry check, adding ~200-800ms to every request (packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the diff adds a token refresh `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` followed by `await prisma.credential.update(...)` immediately after reading `credential.key`, with no conditional/expiry check before doing so. This means constructing/initializing the service will always perform a blocking network call + DB write, which is a concrete performance/architecture concern introduced by the change. The specific latency claim (~200-800ms) isn't verifiable from the diff, but the unconditional refresh behavior is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens external fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no timeout, AbortController, retry, or circuit-breaker, so a slow/hanging sync endpoint blocks all calendar/video operations indefinitely (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when sync is enabled it does `await fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: ... })` with no `signal`/`AbortController` or other timeout mechanism. That’s a concrete resiliency concern introduced by the diff: callers (many calendar/video token refresh paths were changed to use this wrapper) will wait on this network call as long as it takes. The finding’s broader claim about "indefinitely" blocking is somewhat overstated because platform/request-level timeouts aren’t shown in the diff, but the absence of an in-code timeout is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse replaces strict googleCredentialSchema.parse with loose minimumTokenResponseSchema when sync is enabled, then the caller persists the entire mutated unvalidated credential blob, allowing malformed payloads to silently overwrite good credentials and cause a repeated refresh/DB-write loop (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts, packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:92)

adjudication.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService, the code changes from `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` to `parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` and then persists the returned value directly as `key` in Prisma. But `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a Zod `safeParse` result object (`{ success, data, error }`), not the parsed credential data. This means the DB can be updated with the wrapper object instead of the credential payload, corrupting stored credentials. Additionally, when sync is enabled it validates against the looser `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (and may inject a dummy `refresh_token`), so it can overwrite previously valid credentials with a reduced/incorrect shape.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook handler queries prisma.user.findUnique with no field selection (fetches entire user row), and each webhook does 3 sequential DB round trips plus a write with no rate limiting, allowing unbounded work during bulk sync (apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:29)

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler does `prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: reqBody.userId } })` with no `select`, so it will fetch the full user row unnecessarily. The request also performs three sequential DB reads (`user.findUnique`, `app.findUnique`, `credential.findFirst`) followed by a write (`credential.update` or `credential.create`), and there is no rate limiting/throttling logic in this new webhook endpoint—so bulk/abusive calls could cause unbounded DB work. This is a concrete performance/abuse-hardening concern introduced by the diff, but not a clearly verifiable functional correctness defect on its own.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Credential data loss in credential-sharing modes: Zod's minimumTokenResponseSchema strips unknown keys so refresh response only retains access_token, then a literal placeholder "refresh_token" is injected, and callers (Google/office365 CalendarService) persist this to prisma.credential.update, permanently losing the real refresh_token and other credential fields

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when credential sharing is enabled it parses with `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, which does not include `refresh_token`. Since Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, `refresh_token` is dropped, and the function then injects a literal placeholder: `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. Call sites then persist this: e.g. Office365 merges `...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data)` into `o365AuthCredentials` and updates Prisma (`prisma.credential.update`), which would overwrite the real stored refresh token with the placeholder. GoogleCalendarService similarly calls `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` and then stores the result into Prisma, which would also lose the real refresh token (and potentially other fields) in sharing mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses invalid computed keys [z.string().toString()] which evaluate to "[object Object]", second declaration overwrites first, safeParse always fails so every credential-sharing-mode token refresh throws

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` defines computed keys as `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. `z.string()` returns a Zod object, so `.toString()` becomes `"[object Object]"` (and the second key likely collides/overwrites). This makes the schema expect a literal property named `"[object Object]"` rather than accepting arbitrary numeric expiry fields, so `safeParse(response)` will fail for normal OAuth token refresh responses when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is true, causing the refresh path to throw.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Zoho Bigin passes credentialId instead of credential.userId (userId) to refreshOAuthTokens, violating the sync API internal contract
matched_golden_ids: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden and candidate comments identify the same underlying bug: refreshOAuthTokens is being called with credentialId rather than the associated userId (credential.userId), leading to incorrect user lookup and breaking credential sync behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce CalendarService now performs a manual token refresh (network call + DB write) unconditionally on every service construction regardless of token validity or APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, an unflagged behavior change

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, after `const credentialKey = credential.key...`, the code now immediately calls `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` and then `await prisma.credential.update(...)` before creating/returning the `jsforce.Connection`. There is no check for token expiry/validity and no gating on `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED`; this means a refresh network call + DB write will happen whenever this code path runs (i.e., when the service/connection is constructed), which is a significant behavior/perf change visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce refresh uses fragile response.statusText !== "OK" check instead of response.ok/status, so successful refreshes with different statusText throw HttpError 400

Outbound credential-sync request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication (no secret/signature/auth header), allowing arbitrary token issuance requests, unlike the authenticated inbound webhook

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `refreshOAuthTokens`, which when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, performs a POST to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with only a URL-encoded body (`calcomUserId`, `appSlug`) and no auth header/secret/signature (no headers set at all). In contrast, the new inbound webhook handler `/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` explicitly authenticates via a secret header. The finding correctly notes the lack of outbound authentication material, but whether this is a definite defect is not fully provable from the diff since comments say to “Customize the payload based on what your endpoint requires” and the endpoint is self-hosters’ infrastructure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app-credential webhook handler calls appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse outside try/catch, so malformed payloads produce unhandled 500 instead of 400 with meaningful body
matched_golden_ids: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe that `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` can throw on malformed payloads because it's not wrapped in error handling, causing unhandled 500 Internal Server Errors instead of returning an expected 400 Bad Request with a clear response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app-credential webhook crashes on JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(..., "")) when CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is empty string, instead of returning clean 500/403

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler, decryption/JSON.parse only happens after `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED) return 403`. `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (packages/lib/constants.ts). An empty string for `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is falsy, so the handler returns 403 before reaching `symmetricDecrypt(..., process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")`. Therefore the specific crash scenario described (empty string key leading to JSON.parse crash) is not reachable per the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Office365 refresh-error behavior changed from log-and-continue to throwing Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned"), silently aborting calendar operations that previously tolerated partially-malformed responses

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the old code used `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` and, on failure, only `console.error(...)` while continuing (keeping existing `o365AuthCredentials`). The new code calls `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`, whose implementation throws `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` when parsing fails. This is a real behavior change from log-and-continue to throwing/aborting on schema mismatch (though the claim of it being "silently" aborting is debatable since it throws an error).

adjudication_records.issue_text: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is typed as a string (process.env.A && process.env.B evaluates to string, not boolean), so any non-empty value is truthy and pairs badly with the empty encryption-key case

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/constants.ts`, `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is indeed the result of `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, which has type `string | undefined` rather than a strict boolean. However, the claimed bad interaction with an empty encryption key is not supported: if `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is an empty string, the `&&` expression evaluates to `""` (falsy), so sharing is disabled as intended, and all usages in the diff treat it as a truthy/falsy guard.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` fabricates a fake refresh token (literal "refresh_token") when the provider's response omits `refresh_token`, overwriting the real token in the DB and permanently breaking the credential

adjudication.rationale: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` explicitly sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when missing (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts). Callers like Office365 then merge the parsed data into existing credentials (`o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) };` in packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts). If the refreshed-token response (or credential-sync endpoint response) omits `refresh_token`, this code will overwrite the previously stored real refresh token with the literal placeholder, and then persist it via `prisma.credential.update`, breaking future refresh flows when the real refresh token is needed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw fetch Response in sync mode, but Google CalendarService reads `res?.data` which is undefined on a Response, causing TypeError and breaking every Google booking with sync mode enabled

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when sync mode is enabled it does `const response = await fetch(...); return response;`, i.e. it returns a raw `fetch` `Response`. But in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the caller assumes the returned object has a `.data` field: `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;`. A `Response` has no `.data`, so `token` becomes `undefined` and `token.access_token` will throw at runtime when sync mode is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw fetch Response, but Zoho Bigin and Zoho CRM callers access `tokenInfo.data.error` / `tokenInfo.data.expiryDate`, causing crashes or misbehavior

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is truthy, the function executes `fetch(...)` and returns the raw Fetch `Response`. In the Zoho Bigin caller (`packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`), the return value is treated as an Axios response (`tokenInfo.data.error`), and in Zoho CRM (`packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`) it is also treated as Axios (`zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`, `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.expiryDate`). Under the sync-enabled path, these `.data` accesses will be undefined and can cause misbehavior/crashes. The diff clearly introduces this mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw fetch Response, but HubSpot caller expects the `tokensApi.createToken` result object with `.refresh_token`/`.access_token` fields, producing wrong/undefined stored credentials

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, it returns the raw `fetch(...)` `Response` object. However, HubSpot’s `CalendarService` assigns the return value to `hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken` (from `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken(...)`) and will then treat it like a token payload object (e.g., expecting `.access_token`/`.refresh_token` etc.). Under credential-sync mode, that value would instead be a `Response`, so token fields would be missing/undefined and downstream credential update logic would break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Zoho Bigin passes `credentialId` instead of `credential.userId` as `calcomUserId` to `refreshOAuthTokens`, resolving tokens for the wrong or nonexistent user

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credentialId` as the third argument. But `refreshOAuthTokens` is defined as `(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId: number | null)` and, when syncing is enabled, it sends that value as `calcomUserId` in the POST body. Other integrations updated in this diff consistently pass `credential.userId`. Passing a credential record id instead of the user id would cause the sync endpoint to resolve tokens for the wrong/nonexistent user.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Sync-endpoint fetch in `refreshOAuthTokens.ts` has no timeout, no `response.ok` check, no retry, and no error handling, allowing hung or 500-ing endpoints to stall token refresh and booking flows

adjudication.rationale: `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts` adds a new code path that calls `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` and directly returns the resulting Promise/Response without any timeout/AbortController, `response.ok`/status check, or try/catch. Since this function is used in token refresh paths (e.g., Google/Office365/Zoom/Lark/etc.), a slow/hung sync endpoint can cause the awaiting request to hang indefinitely, and 4xx/5xx responses are not handled at this wrapper layer (and may not be consistently handled by all callers), potentially stalling refresh-dependent flows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` which don't act as a catch-all; in credential-sharing mode provider-specific validation (scopes, expiry_date, instance_url, Zoom fields) is bypassed and malformed payloads are persisted

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` attempts to model a catch-all/index signature via computed keys (`[z.string().toString()]`, `[z.string().optional().toString()]`). In Zod, object schemas don’t work this way; those expressions become literal property names (e.g., some stringified representation), not “any string key”, so the schema is not a real catch-all and its validation is incorrect. Additionally, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` explicitly switches to this “minimum” schema when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, which bypasses the provider-specific schema passed in by callers (e.g., Office365/Zoom/Google), meaning provider-specific validation is not applied in that mode and whatever passes the minimal schema can then be used to update persisted credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook handler `app-credential.ts` has no try/catch: `z.parse(req.body)`, `symmetricDecrypt` with a possibly empty `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, and `JSON.parse` of decrypted payload all throw unhandled 500s

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` will throw on invalid input, and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` can throw if decryption fails or the plaintext is not valid JSON. There is no try/catch or `safeParse` handling, so these cases will bubble up as unhandled exceptions and result in 500 responses. The specific claim that `symmetricDecrypt` runs with an empty `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is less grounded because the handler gates on `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` (truthy only when the env var is set), but exceptions from parse/decrypt/JSON.parse are still unhandled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time `!==`; if both `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and the incoming header are undefined the check passes, leaving the credential-write webhook open and vulnerable to overwriting any user's OAuth credentials

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler first blocks requests unless `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is truthy. That constant is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (packages/lib/constants.ts), so if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is undefined (even if the header is also undefined), the route returns 403 before the `!==` comparison is evaluated. Therefore the stated “both undefined passes and leaves it open” condition is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce refresh runs unconditionally on every service instantiation with no token-expiry check, adding a network round-trip and DB write per operation and breaking cached-token usage on Salesforce rate-limit/network failures

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, a refresh-token exchange is now performed immediately after reading `credential.key` (the code calls `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` and then `prisma.credential.update(...)`) with no expiry/validity check before doing so. This does introduce an unconditional network round-trip and DB write along the code path that creates the `jsforce.Connection`. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove this happens on *every* “service instantiation” (depends on how the service is constructed/used elsewhere), nor that it definitively “breaks cached-token usage” (that’s a design/perf/resilience concern rather than a directly verifiable correctness failure from the diff alone).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce uses fragile `response.statusText !== "OK"` check instead of `response.ok`, and the dead `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` check can never trigger because `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on failure

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh call checks `response.statusText !== "OK"` instead of `response.ok`, which is more brittle/less standard but not clearly breaking given typical 200 responses. Also, `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` throws when `safeParse` fails, so the subsequent `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` branch is effectively unreachable dead code (the function only returns a successful SafeParse result).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` gate (WEBHOOK_SECRET && ENCRYPTION_KEY) diverges from runtime requirements (also needs CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT and CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME), with no startup validation or health check, so misconfiguration only fails at runtime in booking flows

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is intentionally derived only from `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (packages/lib/constants.ts). The other envs cited are not runtime requirements for *enabling* the feature in general: `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` is optional (handler defaults to `"calcom-webhook-secret"`), and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is checked separately only in the refresh-token path (`refreshOAuthTokens` / `parseRefreshTokenResponse`) before altering behavior. If the endpoint is missing, code falls back to the normal refresh flow, so the finding’s claim that misconfiguration “only fails at runtime in booking flows” is not verified by the diff, and there is no introduced startup validation/health check code to compare against.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Office365 sync-mode parsing removed the console.error of zod errors, so malformed refresh responses surface as a generic error with no response body logged, hard to debug in production

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the previous `console.error(...)` block that logged the Zod parse error and the raw Microsoft token `responseJson` on `safeParse` failure was removed. The new code calls `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`, which throws `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` on parse failure and does not log the response body. This is an observability/debuggability regression (harder to diagnose malformed refresh responses in production), but not a functional correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Office365 refresh no longer checks `tokenResponse.success` before persisting credentials; minimum schema may return data missing `expiry_date`, persisting stale credentials and defeating the refresh loop

adjudication.rationale: In `Office365CalendarService.refreshAccessToken`, the code now uses `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)` and then merges `tokenResponse.data` into `o365AuthCredentials` (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`). When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` switches to `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, which does not require `expiry_date` (and does not map any numeric expiry field into `expiry_date`). That means the refreshed credential can be persisted without updating `expiry_date`, leaving the old/stale expiry value in place and potentially causing repeated refreshes or incorrect expiry handling. The finding’s statement about not checking `tokenResponse.success` is slightly off because `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on unsuccessful parse, but the underlying issue about missing `expiry_date` being allowed is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full SafeParseResult ({success, data}) but the Google caller persists it directly as the credential key, so the DB stores { success: true, data: {...} } which fails googleCredentialSchema on the next read, breaking Google credential persistence

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the entire Zod `SafeParseResult` object (it `return refreshTokenResponse;` after `safeParse`). In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the caller assigns `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists it directly via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. That would store `{ success: true, data: {...} }` (not just the credential payload) as the credential key, which would not match the expected credential shape on subsequent reads/parsing, breaking persistence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Placeholder string "refresh_token" can overwrite the user's real refresh token when the minimum schema strips it, causing irreversible data loss requiring re-auth

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING is enabled it validates against `minimumTokenResponseSchema` and then forcibly sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` if missing. Downstream code can persist this placeholder and overwrite the real refresh token. For example, in `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the result is spread into `o365AuthCredentials` (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`) and then written back to Prisma, so an absent refresh_token in the response will replace the stored refresh token with the literal placeholder, leading to loss of the real refresh token and requiring re-auth.

adjudication_records.issue_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema computed keys ([z.string().toString()]: z.number()) are dead/broken schema code that don't create the intended 'any property that is a number' and evaluates to a junk literal key, misleading maintainers

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` defines computed keys as `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()`. In a JS object literal this evaluates the expressions immediately, producing a single literal property name (e.g., something like "ZodString" / "[object Object]"), not a pattern like “any key whose value is a number”. As a result, `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` will wrongly require that junk literal key to exist and be a number, causing valid token responses (that typically only have `access_token` and other fields like `expires_in`/`expiry_date`) to fail validation and throw `Invalid refreshed tokens were returned` when credential sharing/sync is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens erases the return type with () => any, hiding that sync mode returns a raw fetch Response while callers expect provider-specific types (HubspotToken, axios tokenInfo with .data), causing type-boundary leaks at all 8 call sites

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` is typed as `(refreshFunction: () => any) => Promise<any>` and in sync mode returns a raw `fetch` `Response` (`return response;`). Several callers still treat the return as provider-specific objects/axios responses, e.g. Google Calendar reads `res?.data` after `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`, Hubspot assigns it to `HubspotToken`, and Zoho Bigin/Zoho CRM access `tokenInfo.data...` after wrapping `axios.post/axios(...)`. In sync mode these will be `Response` objects (no `.data`), causing real runtime breakage and the `any` signature hides this mismatch at compile time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Outbound fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication signature/secret header, making the credential-sync contract unauthenticated and asymmetric with the inbound webhook

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, the code does `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug }) })` with no auth header/signature/secret included. This contrasts with the inbound webhook (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), which explicitly authenticates via a secret header (`CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME`/`CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). The diff therefore introduces an unauthenticated outbound credential-sync request contract as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Zoho Bigin passes credentialId to the sync flow instead of credential.userId, sending the wrong identifier to the sync endpoint which expects a user id

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new sync-aware refresh path calls `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)`. The helper `refreshOAuthTokens`’s third parameter is explicitly `userId: number | null` and is sent as `calcomUserId` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. Passing `credentialId` (inconsistent with other integrations, which pass `credential.userId`) will send the wrong identifier to the sync endpoint, breaking token refresh for Zoho Bigin when the sync flow is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce CalendarService performs an eager blocking token refresh and DB write in the constructor even when the token is valid, coupling construction to side effects

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code now unconditionally performs a refresh-token request (`fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token" ...)`) and then writes the refreshed token into the DB via `prisma.credential.update(...)` before creating the `jsforce.Connection`. There is no check of token validity/expiry before doing this, so construction/connection setup is coupled to network + DB side effects and will happen even if the existing access token is still usable. The diff doesn’t clearly show this is literally inside the class constructor, but it is clearly eager in the connection initialization path shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce checks response.statusText !== "OK" which is unreliable (empty in HTTP/2); response.ok or res.status should be used

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new refresh request checks `if (response.statusText !== "OK")` and throws. `statusText` is not a reliable success indicator for fetch responses (it can differ by environment/protocol and may be empty even on 200), so this can incorrectly throw on successful responses. The diff clearly introduces this behavior; using `response.ok` or `response.status` would avoid false failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook handler: JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) can throw unhandled causing a 500 with no validation, and symmetricDecrypt falls back to || "" instead of a clear 500 when secrets are misconfigured

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), the decrypted payload is parsed with `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` without any try/catch or zod validation of the decrypted structure. If `reqBody.keys` is not valid encrypted JSON (or decrypts to non-JSON), `JSON.parse` will throw and Next.js will return a 500. The note about `symmetricDecrypt(... || "")` causing misconfiguration-related 500s is less directly supported because the handler gates on `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` (which depends on `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`), but the unhandled `JSON.parse` exception is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook handler findFirst({ userId, appId }) won't match legacy credentials with appId: null, creating duplicate credential rows; a type-based fallback would be safer

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), the existing credential lookup is `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId: reqBody.userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })`. If there are any pre-existing/legacy credentials for the same integration that don't have `appId` set to that exact slug (e.g., `appId` is `null` or stored differently), this lookup will miss them and the handler will `create` a new credential row instead of updating, potentially resulting in duplicates. The diff doesn't prove legacy data exists, but the handler as written has no fallback (e.g., by `type`) to avoid that scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: zoho-bigin/api/add.ts hardcodes the slug in the callback URL (WEBAPP_URL + "/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback") instead of using appConfig.slug, adding a second source of truth

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts` changed `redirectUri` from `WEBAPP_URL + `/api/integrations/${appConfig.slug}/callback`` to the hardcoded `WEBAPP_URL + `/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback``. This does create a second source of truth for the slug (code vs `appConfig.slug`). It’s a maintainability/consistency concern, but not a verifiable functional defect in this diff because we can’t confirm `appConfig.slug` is different from `"zoho-bigin"`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a SafeParseReturnType object ({success, data}) instead of the actual credentials, and Google's CalendarService.ts stores this wrapper object directly to credential.key via prisma, destroying stored OAuth credentials for every Google refresh (credential data loss)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the result of `schema.safeParse(...)` (a `SafeParseReturnType` with `{ success, data, error }`), not the parsed token object itself. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code sets `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists it via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. This would store the wrapper object instead of the credentials payload, corrupting `credential.key` on refresh.

adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response in sync mode but callers treat the return as a parsed token object: Hubspot accesses .refresh_token on a Response (undefined), Zoho Bigin and ZohoCRM access tokenInfo.data.error which is undefined, causing silent refresh failure and stale credentials

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch(...)` Response when sync mode is enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`) (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts). Multiple callers still assume the return value is an SDK/axios result or token object: Hubspot assigns it to `HubspotToken` (packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts), Zoho Bigin and ZohoCRM treat it like an axios response and access `.data.error` (packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts, packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts). A `fetch` Response has no `.data`, and it’s not a token object, so in sync mode these refresh paths will break and can leave credentials stale.

adjudication_records.issue_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema in sync mode only validates access_token and zod strips unknown keys by default, so refresh_token, expiry_date, and instance_url are dropped when persisted (Zoom, Office365, Salesforce), permanently breaking integrations once the access token expires

adjudication.rationale: In sync mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), `parseRefreshTokenResponse` uses `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts). `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default (no `.passthrough()`), so fields like `refresh_token`, `expiry_date`, `instance_url`, etc. are removed from the parsed `.data`. The function then forcibly sets `refresh_token` to the literal string "refresh_token" when missing, which will overwrite existing stored refresh tokens in callers that merge/spread parsed data (e.g., Office365: `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`), and can also drop other required fields (e.g., Salesforce update omits `instance_url`). This can break integrations on the next refresh once the real refresh token or other required fields are lost.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse writes the literal placeholder string 'refresh_token' into data.refresh_token when the actual refresh_token is missing, which is later sent as the real OAuth refresh token causing guaranteed auth failures
matched_golden_ids: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same bug: parseRefreshTokenResponse sets data.refresh_token to the literal string 'refresh_token' when the field is missing, which then gets used as a real token and causes authentication/token refresh failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook endpoint app-credential.ts decrypts with process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || '' — if the key is unset, decrypt with empty string either throws unhandled (500) or succeeds unexpectedly

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler, decryption is only reached after `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED) return 403`, and `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (packages/lib/constants.ts). If the encryption key is unset/empty (falsy), the handler exits before calling `symmetricDecrypt(...)`. Therefore the diff does not show a path where an unset key leads to decrypting with `''` and causing an unhandled 500 or unexpected success; the `|| ""` is effectively redundant under the shown guards.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Decrypted keys in the webhook are JSON.parsed with no schema validation and written directly to credential.key for any (userId, appSlug); since the shared secret is the same for all tenants, a caller with the secret can overwrite any user's app credentials (credential-injection surface)

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` allows a caller who knows `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (checked only via a request header) to submit arbitrary `userId` and `appSlug`, and it will `update` or `create` a `credential` for that user/app (`prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId: reqBody.userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })` then `update`/`create`). The decrypted `keys` are `JSON.parse(...)`d and written directly to `credential.key` with no schema validation. This creates a credential-injection/overwrite surface for any user within the instance if the secret is obtained. The claim about “same for all tenants” isn’t provable from the diff, but the overwrite risk for any `userId` on the instance is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on parse failure where callers (Office365 CalendarService.ts, Zoom VideoApiAdapter.ts) previously used safeParse, logged, and continued — making tokenResponse.success checks dead code and turning invalid responses into unhandled exceptions

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `safeParse` failures now immediately `throw new Error(...)` before returning. As a result, callers that still treat the return value as a `safeParse` result (e.g., `Office365CalendarService.ts` does `...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data)` after calling `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)`, and `SalesforceCalendarService.ts` even checks `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` afterward) have effectively dead/unreachable `*.success` checks. The diff also removes Office365’s prior non-throwing/logging behavior on parse failure, but whether this new throwing behavior is a functional bug vs. an intentional stricter failure mode can’t be conclusively determined from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce CalendarService performs an unconditional token refresh in the constructor on every service instantiation (per-operation network call, rate-limit exposure, single point of failure) instead of jsforce's lazy refresh

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an immediate refresh-token network call in `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts` before creating the `jsforce.Connection`: it `fetch`es `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token`, parses, and then updates Prisma (`prisma.credential.update(...)`) unconditionally during service initialization (right after `const credentialKey = ...`). This means every instantiation triggers a per-operation token refresh and DB write, which is a reliability/perf/rate-limit concern rather than a clear functional defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Salesforce refresh checks response.statusText !== 'OK' which is locale/server-dependent instead of using response.ok
matched_golden_ids: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core problem: the OAuth token refresh logic relies on `response.statusText` (specifically comparing to 'OK') which is unreliable/locale or server dependent, and should use `response.ok` to correctly detect success.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Zoho Bigin CalendarService.ts passes credentialId where the helper expects credential.userId, causing sync mode to be silently never used or a ReferenceError, so the sync-enabled path can pass while real sync never fires

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credentialId` as the third argument, but `refreshOAuthTokens` is defined as `(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId: number | null)` and uses that value as `calcomUserId` in the sync-mode request body. All other integrations in the diff pass `credential.userId`. If `credentialId` is the credential record id (as the name implies), sync-mode would send the wrong user identifier (and potentially enable the sync path incorrectly), which is broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT sends no auth header/secret and never checks response.ok or non-2xx status, and sends (userId, appSlug) in plaintext; error/garbage responses are returned to callers as valid tokens

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` it does `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug }) })` with no auth/secret header and no `response.ok`/status handling, then returns the raw `Response`. Multiple callers expect provider-shaped token objects / axios-like responses (e.g. Hubspot: `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`; Google: uses `res?.data`), so non-2xx/garbage responses (or even just the wrong response type) can propagate and break token refresh behavior, and the sync endpoint call itself is unauthenticated in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TOCTOU race in webhook credential create/update: findFirst then create is not atomic, so concurrent webhooks for the same user/app create duplicate credentials, leaving a stale duplicate that bookings may still use

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler does a non-atomic `findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` followed by either `credential.update` or `credential.create`. If two webhook requests for the same `userId`/`appSlug` run concurrently, both can observe “no credential” and both execute `create`, producing duplicates unless the database enforces a unique constraint on `(userId, appId)` (not shown in this diff). The code comment (“Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id”) suggests no suitable unique key is being relied on, making the race plausible and a real defect risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed key [z.string().toString()] evaluates to the literal key '[ZodString]' (a required number field) rather than allowing other properties as the comment claims — a misleading guard that appears to validate more than it does

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. These expressions evaluate immediately to a literal string (the Zod schema object's string representation), so the resulting Zod object schema only defines a property with that literal name, not “any string key”. This means the comment/intent (“assume any property with a number is the expiry” / “allow other properties”) is not implemented and the guard validates far less/differently than claimed. Correct approaches would be `z.record(...)` or `z.object({...}).catchall(...)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook secret compared with !== (timing-unsafe, not constant-time comparison), and CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME taken raw from env so uppercase/normalized values silently miss causing all requests to 403

adjudication.rationale:
In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the webhook secret is validated via a direct string inequality check:
```ts
req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET
```
This is timing-unsafe (not constant-time) for secret comparison. Also, Node/Next normalizes incoming header keys to lowercase in `req.headers`; since `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` is used verbatim (not lowercased), providing a mixed/uppercased env value will fail to find the header and cause all requests to 403. The `.env.example` comment acknowledges this risk (“Should be in lowercase”), but the code doesn’t enforce it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Body schema parse at app-credential.ts:36 throws unhandled ZodError on malformed payloads, producing a 500 with stack trace instead of a 400

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler calls `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` without any try/catch or safeParse handling. A malformed payload will throw a `ZodError`, which (in a Next.js API route) results in an unhandled exception and a 500 response rather than a controlled 400-level validation error. This behavior is directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is derived via process.env.X && process.env.Y string truthiness, so setting a var to a non-empty but meaningless value like 'false' enables sharing

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/constants.ts`, `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY;`, which relies on string truthiness rather than an explicit boolean. That means values like `"false"` (non-empty) will still enable the feature. This directly gates sensitive behavior in the new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) and token-refresh routing (`refreshOAuthTokens` / `parseRefreshTokenResponse`), so an operator intending to disable by setting env vars to `false` could inadvertently enable credential sharing with a weak/guessable secret.
